title: Low-rank approximation: Schatten residual and right projection.
summary: Construct a rank-$k$ orthogonal right projection $P$ approximating the optimal rank-$k$ residual.

task.description_zh: Construct a rank-$k$ orthogonal right projection $P$ approximating the optimal rank-$k$ residual.
description_paragraphs: Construct a rank-$k$ orthogonal right projection $P$ approximating the optimal rank-$k$ residual.

model.instance: The unknown real matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ is arbitrary, with $d_{\mathrm{min}}=\min(m,n)$, $1\le k<d_{\mathrm{min}}$, and $1\le p\le\infty$. The parameter k restricts output rank only.

assumptions.description: No eigengap, full-rank, or low-rank promise is imposed; a zero optimal tail is included in the model.

model.description_zh: The matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ is arbitrary and real, with $d_{\mathrm{min}}=\min\{m,n\}$, $1\le k<d_{\mathrm{min}}$, and $1\le p\le\infty$. No bound on actual rank, singular-value gap, or spectral decay is promised.

oracle.query_domain_description: Right products map R^n to R^m; transpose products map R^m to R^n. A q-column block costs q queries. Entries, inverse actions, shifted solves, and matrix-function actions are not additional free feedback.
oracle.description_zh: Inputs $m,n,k,p,\varepsilon$ are public and $A$ hidden. Exact $Av$ at arbitrary $v\in\mathbb R^n$ and exact $A^{\mathsf T}u$ at arbitrary $u\in\mathbb R^m$ are allowed and charged separately.
description_paragraphs: The information $m,n,k,p,\varepsilon$ is public and $A$ is hidden. Exact $Av$ is available for every $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$, and exact $A^{\mathsf T}u$ for every $u\in\mathbb{R}^m$. The two directions are charged separately.

output.feasibility: A real rank-$k$ orthogonal projection $P\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, with $P=P^{\mathsf T}=P^2$, encodable by an $n\times k$ orthonormal basis.
output.allowed_postprocessing: Arbitrary admissible postprocessing; the output need not have appeared as a query vector.
output.certificate_requirement: Only the true-loss guarantee is required; no computable certificate is requested.
output.description_zh: Return $P\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ satisfying $P=P^{\mathsf T}=P^2$ and $\operatorname{rank}(P)=k$, or an orthonormal basis for that projector. Neither $AP$ nor an error certificate is required.
description_paragraphs: Return $P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ satisfying $P=P^{\mathsf T}=P^2$ and $\operatorname{rank}(P)=k$, or an orthonormal basis for that projector. Neither $AP$ nor an error certificate is required.

metric.normalization: If both numerator and denominator are zero, the loss is zero. A zero denominator with nonzero numerator gives +∞. Otherwise use the stated ratio.
metric.finiteness_conditions: The specified dimension is finite, and the model and spectral assumptions hold.
metric.description_zh: For finite $p$, use $\|M\|_{S_p}=(\sum_i\sigma_i(M)^p)^{1/p}$; $p=\infty$ gives the spectral norm. Define $\operatorname{OPT}_{p,k}=\min_{\operatorname{rank}(B)\le k}\|A-B\|_{S_p}$. Success means $\|A(I_n-P)\|_{S_p}\le(1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}_{p,k}$. A zero optimal residual requires exact recovery of the relevant row space. The unsquared error criterion is retained.

bounds.hidden_constants: The constant $C$ is uniform in $m,n,k,p,\epsilon$. The quantities $c_B,C_{\mathrm{bridge}},\alpha_B$ are fixed universal proof constants.
bounds.derivation: Let $\alpha_B=\min\{1/2,c_B/(2C_{\mathrm{bridge}})\}$ and run BCW with internal tolerance $\delta_B=\alpha_B\varepsilon$. If $p\varepsilon\le C_{\mathrm{bridge}}\log d_{\mathrm{min}}$, then $p\le c_B\log(d_{\mathrm{min}})/\delta_B$, while $\delta_B\le\varepsilon/2<1$. The source residual guarantee $(1+\delta_B)$ therefore implies the target $(1+\varepsilon)$ guarantee. Substituting $\delta_B$ into the query bound gives $N\le Ck\log(2d_{\mathrm{min}}/\varepsilon)[p^{1/6}\varepsilon^{-1/3}+\sqrt p]$. Since $\alpha_B$ is fixed in advance, the constants are uniform in varying p. When $m<n$, run the algorithm on $A^{\mathsf T}$ and include at most k additional $A^{\mathsf T}U$ calls to form the right projector. The resulting right subspace may be enlarged to rank k, which can only decrease the residual.

bounds.derivation:
Run the Musco-Musco block Krylov algorithm at internal spectral tolerance $\eta=\varepsilon/4$. The iteration count is $$
O\bigl(\varepsilon^{-1/2}\log(2d_{\mathrm{min}}/\varepsilon)\bigr).
$$ Charging each column separately and including the output conversion gives $$
N\le Ck\varepsilon^{-1/2}\log(2d_{\mathrm{min}}/\varepsilon).
$$ This branch requires $p\ge C_{\mathrm{bridge}}\log(d_{\mathrm{min}})/\varepsilon$, hence $d_{\mathrm{min}}^{1/p}\le1+\varepsilon/4$. Using $\operatorname{rank}(A(I_n-P))\le d_{\mathrm{min}}$ yields $$
\begin{aligned}
\|A(I_n-P)\|_{S_p}
&\le(1+\varepsilon/4)^2\operatorname{OPT}_{\infty,k}\\
&\le(1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}_{p,k}.
\end{aligned}
$$

bracket.envelope_certificate: Compare the bound of each complete algorithm with reconstruction in $d_{\mathrm{min}}$ queries, where $d_{\mathrm{min}}=\min\{m,n\}$ corresponds to the source dimension notation $N$. Three cases cover the full declared region. If $p\varepsilon\le1$, then $\sqrt p\le p^{1/6}\varepsilon^{-1/3}$. If $1\le p\varepsilon\le C_{\mathrm{bridge}}\log d_{\mathrm{min}}$, both BCW terms are bounded by $\varepsilon^{-1/2}\operatorname{polylog}(d_{\mathrm{min}})$. If $p\ge C_{\mathrm{bridge}}\log(d_{\mathrm{min}})/\varepsilon$, the spectral-norm conversion applies. Constants depending on fixed $p$ remain explicit; the $\sqrt p$ term growing with $p$ is retained. After rescaling BCW's internal tolerance, the first case incurs $\log(2d_{\mathrm{min}}/\varepsilon)$, the second adds at most $\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{bridge}}\log d_{\mathrm{min}}}$, and the third uses the single-logarithm spectral bound. With $\Phi_{\mathrm{lr}}(p,\varepsilon)=\min\{p^{1/6}\varepsilon^{-1/3},\varepsilon^{-1/2}\}$, this gives $Q_{\mathrm{upper}}\le\min\{d_{\mathrm{min}},Ck\Phi_{\mathrm{lr}}(p,\varepsilon)\log(2d_{\mathrm{min}}/\varepsilon)\sqrt{\log(2d_{\mathrm{min}})}\}$. The minimum includes only applicable branches. BCW's parameter window is enforced using $\delta_B=\alpha_B\varepsilon$ with the stated rescaling constant; it cannot be dropped by silently changing hidden constants.

proofs.title: Deterministic basis reconstruction, choosing the smaller row or column direction.
proofs.body: Recover all columns in $n$ right queries or all rows in $m$ transpose queries, choosing the cheaper channel. Exact internal singular-value decomposition returns the orthogonal right projection onto the leading $k$ right singular vectors. The singular-value characterization of the best rank-$k$ Schatten approximation shows that the residual is optimal for the declared norm order, including zero optimal residual. The query count is $\min\{m,n\}$; the two alternatives are complete algorithms, not a coordinatewise combination of budgets.
proofs.scope: All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.

evidence.supports: Block Krylov at accuracy eta has q=O(log(d)/sqrt(eta)) iterations and returns a relative (1+eta) spectral residual with probability 99/100. Counting every vector in Krylov construction and Q postprocessing gives O(k q) exact two-sided products. Conservative bound O(k eta^-1/2 log(2d/eta)) is sufficient here.
notes: Original arXiv v4 PDF read from author MIT mirror. Query-count derivation counts every block column; arithmetic costs remain uncharged. The new Schatten lower theorem was not independently reproved.
For rectangular matrices choose an orientation with the smaller dimension on the right; the LR26 section9 projector conversion adds at most k products.
